rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so the decision hinges on study archetype, PRS-comparable performance evidence, and covariate comparability. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation; Million Veteran Program context) with a clear direct endpoint (prevalent AAA) and provides a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), whereas several others mainly report full-model discrimination metrics that are not PRS-only. The main limitation is that PGS000753 is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, while multiple newer genome-wide PRS-CS/LDpred2 models exist; however, those alternatives either come from framework/portability papers (PGS001784, PGS002054) or report only full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown covariates (PGS003972/PGS003973), making their apparent discrimination less directly comparable to standalone PRS performance. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS003973 and PGS003972 are disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis-derived PRS-CS scores (Nat Genet) with direct endpoints but only full-model metrics and unknown/limited covariate transparency; PGS002054 (LDpred2) and PGS001784 (PRS-CS-auto) provide PRS-comparable R2/partial-r but are penalized as portability/framework-style scores despite exact trait matching. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo/phenotyping alignment to alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder. PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder", uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), is developed from multi-cohort sources (MVP, UKB), and reports a relatively strong discriminative effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a sizable EUR evaluation (n=7,900). Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUC/R2; covariates are unknown for PGS002738, reducing comparability and keeping confidence below high. Runners-up: PGS002739 is also an alcohol dependence EFO match with an OR top 10% vs rest of 1.76 (1.32–2.34) but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean ancestry and uses a very small gene-based score (858 variants), making it less generally supported without a specified deployment ancestry. PGS000201 and PGS000202 are close direct matches (trait_efo="alcohol dependence measurement"; DSM-5 AUD criteria count) and use PRS-CS with very large variant counts, but their reported incremental ΔR² values are smaller (0.01192 and 0.00456 respectively) and they appear UKB-based with less multi-cohort support; between them, PGS000201 is stronger than PGS000202 due to higher ΔR² and larger validation n (7,599 vs 1,251).

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are near-synonymous alcoholic/alcohol-associated cirrhosis labels). No candidate reports clearly PRS-only AUROC; reported AUROC/C-index values are full-model metrics and thus not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence per the provided domain guidance, which limits confidence.

PGS004913 is preferred because it is disease-focused (publication explicitly about an alcohol-associated cirrhosis PRS among heavy drinkers), has clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and provides PRS-comparable signal via an R²=0.029 plus an OR (top vs bottom deciles)=4.4, giving more direct PRS-specific evidence than the others.

Runner-up PGS001777 is also disease-focused and shows strong stratification (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18), but it is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, and a small validation sample (n=1,390), making robustness less supported from the visible metadata.

PGS000704 ranks behind because it appears to come from a broad biomarker genetics paper (less clearly disease-focused for alcoholic cirrhosis), and its main reported discrimination is a full-model C-index=0.711 with only moderate HR per SD (1.18), which is weaker PRS-specific evidence despite large UKB-based sample sizes.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris by trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (Angina / I20 ICD10 / PheCode 411.3 / TTE angina). The strongest visible PRS-comparable evidence comes from the UKB snpnet models (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262), which report PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC ~0.58 and PGS R2 ~0.012–0.013) that are plausibly below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.009–0.014; liability ~0.134), and also report incremental AUROC (~0.008–0.010), allowing interpretation of PRS contribution rather than relying on covariate-driven full-model AUROC. Among these, PGS001262 is preferred because it has the highest reported PGS-only AUROC (0.58683), highest PGS-only R2 (0.01304), and highest incremental AUROC (0.0098) within this coherent endpoint family, with standard/basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a larger validation n (49,472) than its close siblings.

However, confidence is not High because (i) these snpnet scores come from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk despite clean metadata, and (ii) several newer PheCode-based MVP models (PGS005048–PGS005059) show higher full-model C-index (~0.76) and strong per-SD ORs (~1.43–1.49 for some), but they do not report PGS-only discrimination, making them harder to compare directly and raising the possibility that their apparent advantage is partly covariate-driven. The 2024 Commun Biol I20 models (PGS004457/PGS004527) also lack PRS-comparable metrics beyond OR, further limiting decisive separation.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=ankylosing spondylitis; phenotyping_reported is ankylosing spondylitis or a closely related TTE formulation), so a direct-match exists. PGS001267 is selected as best supported because it reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS-only R2 (0.0988), plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), enabling the cleanest within-pool interpretability; its PRS-only R2 is also well below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.399), passing the sanity check. However, confidence is not high because the two strongest-metric candidates (PGS001267/PGS001268) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (explicitly cautioned as often less externally robust), while other direct-match candidates are from a portability framework (PGS002089/PGS001876) with only partial-correlation metrics (not directly comparable to AUROC/R2) and an East Asian-only study family (PGS003420–PGS003424) reporting only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,298), limiting cross-candidate comparability. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001268 (similar endpoint with slightly higher reported metrics but time-to-event phenotyping penalty), then PGS002089 (higher partial-r than PGS001876 and genome-wide method/variant count), then PGS001876, then the strongest of the EAS-only full-model-AUROC set (PGS003420).

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) plus closely aligned aortic valve function measurement scores whose phenotyping is still incident aortic stenosis (PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases), a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with high variant count (~1.12M), and it reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (multiple cardiometabolic comorbidities and exposures), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated from the visible metadata. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis score with a strong HR (1.64) and large genome-wide variant count but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS005255 and PGS005256 have trait labels as valve-function measurements but share the same incident aortic stenosis phenotyping and show moderate HRs (~1.53), making them plausible but less directly aligned by trait_reported; among the remaining non-aortic-stenosis models, PGS004911 is included last only to fill the required list, but it is a different disease (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) and thus has weak direct-match support for aortic stenosis. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including exact EFO matches (PGS001135: “Arthritis (nos)” with trait_efo=arthritis; PGS004477/PGS004547: “M13 (Other arthritis)” with trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is selected as best because it has the cleanest direct phenotype alignment to generic arthritis (nos) and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.53928; PGS-only R2=0.00291) plus incremental AUROC (0.00314), enabling interpretation of PRS contribution rather than relying only on full-model discrimination. However, confidence is limited because PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused models in external validation; additionally, other exact-EFO arthritis models (PGS004477/PGS004547) exist but lack comparable PRS-only metrics, making them hard to rank above/below PGS001135 on visible evidence alone. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004477 and PGS004547 are exact-EFO arthritis models but with sparse performance reporting (only ORs, unknown covariates); then broader but still arthritis-direct clinical entities (PGS000114 juvenile idiopathic arthritis; PGS000342 psoriatic arthritis) are included as additional direct arthritis-spectrum matches with explicit arthritis endpoints, though they are subtype-specific rather than generic arthritis.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable evidence. PGS002727 is preferred because it is explicitly a disease-focused pediatric asthma PRS (phenotyping_reported: Pediatric asthma) with strong PRS-discrimination evidence via per-SD effect size (OR=1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) and a reported AUROC (0.66 with CI), and it is evaluated in a very large sample (n=391,820). Its main limitation is endpoint specificity (pediatric asthma rather than generic asthma) and unknown covariates, which reduces certainty for general asthma risk.

Runners-up: PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; AUROC 0.659; Nagelkerke R2 0.048844 covariates-regressed-out) has strong PRS-comparable R2 evidence but is from a global-biobank framework-style paper and has smaller EUR eval (n=7,128). PGS001787 has similarly framework-style provenance with weaker PRS R2 (0.035168) despite huge evaluation size (n=351,578), so it ranks below PGS001782. PGS001344 has strong endpoint fidelity (doctor-diagnosed asthma) and good reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.66621) but comes from the pan-trait UKB snpnet framework and its AUROC is not clearly PRS-only. PGS002061 (LDpred2; partial correlation 0.1184) is a UKB portability framework score with PRS-like metric but lacks clearer PRS-only AUROC/R2 and is less directly informative than the above. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo includes atopic eczema). Ranking is driven primarily by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported) and then by available PRS-comparable evidence and structural/method signals.

Best: PGS002755 is the strongest direct-match because it targets incident atopic dermatitis (clean disease endpoint) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), with a large EUR evaluation (n=337,910) and a reported HR (high vs low PRS)=1.249 (1.123–1.391). Main limitation: no PRS-only AUROC/R² is reported, so effect-size evidence is the main quantitative support.

Runners-up: (1) PGS004587 also uses an incident atopic dermatitis endpoint with EUR evaluation and HR=1.153 (1.037–1.282), but is structurally weaker (23 GWAS-significant SNPs) and has smaller effect size. (2) PGS001773 is disease-focused (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis) but is severity-restricted and reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates; without PGS-only metrics this high AUROC is not directly comparable and may be covariate-driven (and the reported R² exceeds the provided heritability ceiling, raising comparability concerns). (3–4) PGS003486 and PGS003459 are further penalized because their phenotyping is paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients (therapy/context-specific endpoint), despite reporting modest full-model AUROCs (~0.57–0.59) and ORs; between them, PGS003486 is slightly preferred due to higher OR (1.89 vs 1.83) and similar endpoint/covariates.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the top candidates lack PRS-only discrimination metrics and several alternatives have endpoint restrictions (severity- or treatment-induced phenotypes), limiting a clearly high-confidence direct-match recommendation.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable evidence and study archetype. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused AF meta-analysis score (Nat Genet 2025) with a direct AF endpoint and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663), and it is supported by many performance records (45), suggesting more robust evaluation than most alternatives in the visible list. Main limitation: the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric (covariates include CHARGE-AF), and no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided here, so the incremental PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across models.

Runners-up: PGS005313 is also a recent disease-focused multi-cohort AF model with strong OR (1.82) and AUROC 0.78, but it is evaluated in a MAE-only setting (per ancestry_distribution) which is a transportability limitation relative to the EUR-evaluated best pick. PGS002814 has extremely large GWAS training (n=1,150,799) and strong OR (~1.94) with AUROC 0.74, but it is developed in MAE and evaluated in EAS only, making it less generally supported without a specified deployment ancestry. PGS000016 (Nat Genet 2019) is a classic genome-wide LDpred AF score with explicit PRS-only R2 (0.029), which is directly comparable and below the AF heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.020–0.031), but its headline AUROC (0.77) is full-model and it is older/single-biobank-developed (UKB). PGS000331 (Nat Med 2020) is disease-focused with incident AF and HR 1.62 and C-index 0.751, but has smaller training (n=21,813) and less compelling metric support than the higher-supported meta-analysis-based candidates. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (atrial flutter appears in trait_reported/trait_efo for each), but 3/4 are composite endpoints (“atrial fibrillation and flutter”), reducing endpoint specificity for flutter alone. PGS001263 is the only model with an exact atrial flutter phenotype/label alignment (trait_reported, trait_efo, phenotyping_reported all “Atrial flutter”) and it reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R2=0.025, which is below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443) and therefore not obviously inconsistent. However, it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk; this prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ designation. Among runners-up, PGS001339 is closest on evidence (same framework family and similar PRS-only metrics) but uses a time-to-event composite endpoint (“TTE atrial fibrillation and flutter”), adding endpoint mismatch. PGS002050 and PGS001841 (UKB portability framework) have potentially stronger method/structure signals (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage; penalized regression) and larger training n, but they lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 in the visible metrics (only partial-r), making them harder to rank confidently against the snpnet models for this specific target.

Two direct-match candidates are present for autism spectrum disorder (ASD): PGS000327 and PGS002790. PGS000327 is best supported because its phenotype fields are fully aligned (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ASD), it comes from an ASD-focused publication (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”), and it reports supportive PRS signal via effect size (OR=1.33 per SD) plus an R²-like metric (full_model_r2=0.0245) with only basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). In contrast, PGS002790 has a notable endpoint-fidelity concern: phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)” despite trait_reported being ASD, making it less coherent as a direct ASD diagnosis endpoint; it also shows weaker reported variance explained (partial R²≈0.00546) and lacks effect-size reporting. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because neither model provides clearly PRS-comparable (PGS-only) AUC/R², and the runner-up has an explicit phenotype mismatch/withdrawn phenotype label that limits confidence.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). The strongest-supported choice is PGS000452 because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates only (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest visible performance/effect evidence among the comparable MGI-evaluated siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), Nagelkerke R² 0.0487, and a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) plus strong top-1% vs rest OR 3.61. Runners-up are selected from the same coherent Cancer PRSweb family with the same endpoint/covariates/ancestry context and very similar metrics: PGS000454 (AUROC 0.632; R² 0.0489; OR 1.661; top-1% OR 3.79), PGS000456 (AUROC 0.63; R² 0.0456; OR 1.633; top-1% OR 3.95), and PGS000458 (AUROC 0.628; R² 0.0457; OR 1.634; top-1% OR 4.03). Confidence is Moderate because several near-clone Cancer PRSweb candidates (notably PGS000452 vs PGS000454) are essentially indistinguishable on the visible evidence, and all reported AUROCs here are full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), limiting comparability across studies per the provided domain guidance. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

PGS000924 is ranked behind due to being a pan-trait UKB framework score (813-traits sparse snpnet) and using a time-to-event endpoint; its very high reported R2/AUROC also conflicts with the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.089), raising comparability/sanity-check concerns. Direct-match candidates are present (3 models with trait_reported/trait_efo mapping to bipolar disorder and bipolar I/II). However, all three have endpoint-fidelity concerns because phenotyping_reported fields are not bipolar diagnosis endpoints (they reference cognitive/behavioral measures), and none reports PRS-comparable discrimination (no AUC/PRS-only R2; only small partial R² values). With method_name (SDPR), ancestry (EUR-only GWAS/EVAL), publication family, covariates (age, PCs1-3), and overall metadata essentially identical across candidates, there is no strong evidence-based differentiator; PGS002786 is selected only because it is the closest concept match to the target trait label (bipolar disorder vs subtype-specific I/II). All three candidates are direct matches at the broad target level (coagulation disorders), but none is an exact, clearly high-fidelity match to the generic umbrella label “blood coagulation disease,” and the evidence is limited/incomparable across candidates. PGS002034 is preferred because it targets a specific coagulation disease entity (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency; phenotyping matches the reported trait) and, within its same-endpoint/same-publication sibling pair, it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), while showing essentially identical partial-correlation performance (partial-r ~0.0563 vs ~0.0562) under similar ancestry context (DEV EUR; EVAL EUR/SAS). PGS001826 is the closest runner-up as the near-clone sibling with nearly identical endpoint and performance but a smaller, more limited variant set. PGS001033 is ranked below both because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”) with an extremely sparse 1-variant model and a time-to-event phenotype; although it reports AUROC metrics, domain guidance cautions that framework sparse scores often generalize poorly and that full-model AUROC should not be over-weighted. Overall confidence is low because the target is broad while two candidates are narrow congenital deficiencies and the only broadly labeled candidate is a framework sparse TTE model, leaving no clearly strong, endpoint-faithful, disease-focused option in the visible list. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for the target trait (breast carcinoma / breast cancer). The strongest-supported option in the visible list is PGS004153 because it is a direct breast cancer endpoint (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer), uses a multi-score aggregation method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; a positive structural signal per provided domain knowledge), and reports strong standalone discrimination evidence in a large European evaluation (AUROC=0.6625 with R²=0.0764 and OR per SD ~1.83; covariates explicitly 0, reducing concern that performance is covariate-driven). Runners-up are other direct breast cancer models from the same five-biobank evaluation family with similarly clean covariates (0) and strong AUROC/R²/OR evidence, but slightly lower reported discrimination than PGS004153: PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV; AUROC~0.6598, R²~0.0739), PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto; AUROC~0.6598, R²~0.0736), PGS004083 (PRS-CS-auto; AUROC~0.6553, R²~0.0697), and PGS004069 (megaprs.CV; AUROC~0.6558, R²~0.0709). Confidence is Moderate because multiple top candidates are near-tied within the same endpoint/validation context and differences are modest, so the choice relies on the limited visible metrics rather than a clearly dominant external-validation advantage.

Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001301 reports explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.82867; PGS R2 no covariates=0.14224) but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper and uses a broader phenotype label (Malabsorption/coeliac disease). PGS000040 shows very high AUROC (0.9) but only as full-model with unknown covariates and smaller validation (n=2,476). PGS000042 and PGS000041 are phenotype-restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (endpoint mismatch vs generic celiac disease) despite moderate full-model AUROC (~0.73). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are cervical cancer, mostly incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is best supported overall because it comes from a cervical-phenotype-focused GWAS meta-analysis study (publication explicitly about cervical phenotypes and risk stratification), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555), and reports a moderate HR per SD (1.33) with basic covariates (age, smoking) and EUR evaluation—together providing the strongest structural and endpoint-faithful evidence in this set. Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 have strong endpoint fidelity (incident cervical cancer) and large EUR evaluation (n=211,795) with similar HR (~1.21–1.22), but their reported discrimination is full-model and they are sparse GWAS-hit scores (10 variants), limiting standalone PRS evidence; PGS005165 is ancestry-specific (EAS-only) with modest HR (1.2) and modest C-index (0.566), making it less generally supported absent a specified deployment ancestry; PGS003389 has weak reported discrimination (AUROC 0.563; R² 0.00158) despite being genome-wide (lassosum, 2,814 variants). All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or the closely aligned composite “cholelithiasis and cholecystitis”). The main limitation is that several candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R², and the partial-r metric is not directly comparable to the AUROC/R² reported for PGS001174; additionally, PGS002072 comes from a UKB portability framework paper, which domain guidance flags as generally weaker than disease-focused studies, but no clearly disease-focused multi-cohort alternative is present in this candidate list. Runners-up: PGS001861 is the same endpoint/publication family with a slightly lower partial-r (0.0948) and a penalized regression method; PGS004546 and PGS004476 are exact K80 cholelithiasis endpoints with moderate per-SD ORs (1.30 and 1.22) but have unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable discrimination metrics; PGS001174 reports explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC but is from the “813 traits” sparse UKB framework (snpnet, 970 variants) and uses a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals in the provided domain guidance. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo=chronic kidney disease, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how interpretable their reported performance is as PRS-specific. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused (Nat Med: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”), uses a clear clinical CKD definition (stage 3+ / eGFR<45), has large development (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65). Its main limitation is that the reported AUROC (0.78) is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so PRS-only discrimination cannot be directly compared across models.

Runners-up: (1) PGS005090 has very strong reported metrics (AUROC=0.9; R²=0.1; OR=1.41) and a CKD stage 3+ framing, but it is AFR-only (GWAS/EVAL AFR) and the very high full-model AUROC may not be PRS-only; (2) PGS004158 is an ensemble/multi-PRS (“UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV”) with the best full-model AUROC among the five-biobank method-evaluation siblings (AUROC≈0.592) and clean covariates (0), but it is from a benchmarking family with modest discrimination and not a dedicated CKD prediction study; (3) PGS005113 is CKDGen-based and reports a moderate OR=1.35 with broad evaluation ancestries, but lacks PRS-only metrics and is embedded in a proteomic-marker context; (4) PGS004030 (LDpred2-auto) is the strongest single-method sibling in the same five-biobank family by AUROC/R² (AUROC≈0.589; R²≈0.0187; covariates 0), but remains modest and close to near-clones, so tie-breaking is weak.

All 10 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, with strongest endpoint fidelity for those explicitly labeled COPD/J44/chronic airway obstruction.
